classification.difficultyReason: Justify a compass construction using SSS and conclude that corresponding angles are equal.

content.prompt:
This question provides a proof of the angle bisector construction.

The arcs intersecting at $M$ are centred at $P$ and $Q$.

spec.description: Angle AOB with P and Q on its rays, a ray OM extending beyond M, an arc centred at O through P and Q, and equal-radius construction arcs centred at P and Q meeting at M. PM and QM are absent.
spec.mathematics: OP=OQ and PM=QM are construction relationships. M lies inside angle AOB. Coordinates determine consistent compass arcs without supplying numerical measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original rays, construction arcs, point markers and labels are visible; the requested joins and proof are withheld.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Copy the diagram and join the intervals $PM$ and $QM$.

answer.worked: Copy the construction and draw the straight intervals $PM$ and $QM$, forming $\triangle PMO$ and $\triangle QMO$.

spec.description: Complete construction with PM and QM joined; all original rays, arcs and labels retained.
spec.mathematics: The joins expose triangles PMO and QMO sharing OM.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution-only joins PM and QM are visible.

answer.worked:
$OP=OQ$ because they are radii of the same circle centred at $O$.

$PM=QM$ because the construction arcs centred at $P$ and $Q$ use the same compass radius.

$OM=OM$ is a common side.

Therefore $\triangle PMO\equiv\triangle QMO$ (SSS).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence explain why $OM$ is the bisector of $\angle AOB$.

answer.short: $\angle POM=\angle QOM$ by congruence, so $OM$ bisects $\angle AOB$.
answer.worked:
$\angle POM=\angle QOM$ because corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal.

Since $P$ lies on $OA$ and $Q$ lies on $OB$, $\angle AOM=\angle MOB$.

Therefore $OM$ bisects $\angle AOB$.
